headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: CrewAI’s writable workspace and broad egress can expose Chatwoot customer data if outputs are reused without verification.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Chatwoot has broad network egress and exposes support content, while CrewAI reads/writes the host working directory and uses stdin/stdout. If Chatwoot outputs are copied into CrewAI tasks or files, prompt-like content can be treated as instructions. The shared-file path is plausible, but not proven by docs alone.
conditions: IF Chatwoot outputs are written into CrewAI task files or prompts, injection becomes plausible.
IF the operator manually copies support transcripts from Chatwoot into CrewAI, the bridge exists.
mitigations: Separate Chatwoot exports from CrewAI working directories.
Use a strict prompt template that strips user-authored instructions.
Add a human review step before any CrewAI task consumes Chatwoot text.
Disable automatic file ingestion for CrewAI runs.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags and content filtering between systems.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Chatwoot touches customer data, contact profiles, interaction history, orders, and messages. CrewAI can read/write the host filesystem and send data to model providers or configured tools over broad egress. In a shared workspace, Chatwoot data can be copied into CrewAI and then leave to third parties by default-like tool use, creating a realistic leakage path.
conditions: IF Chatwoot exports or logs are placed in CrewAI's working directory, CrewAI can read them.
IF CrewAI tools or model providers receive those files, the data can egress externally.
mitigations: Keep Chatwoot data outside CrewAI's working directory.
Restrict CrewAI tool access to non-sensitive datasets.
Turn off or gate any file-reading tasks in CrewAI.
Use a separate service account and isolated storage.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP and per-path access controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Chatwoot is a customer-support app with integrations, while CrewAI can execute shell commands, spawn subprocesses, and write the filesystem. Their capabilities overlap on mutable host resources, so concurrent runs can overwrite or corrupt shared files if pointed at the same directory. The profiles do not show locking or coordination primitives, so the conflict is plausible in default host setups.
conditions: IF both agents target the same host directory, writes can collide.
IF Chatwoot integration artifacts are edited while CrewAI runs shell/file tasks, state corruption is possible.
mitigations: Assign separate directories for each agent.
Run CrewAI in a container with a private volume.
Avoid concurrent writes to shared artifacts.
Use file locks for any shared outputs.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: CrewAI is a multi-agent orchestration layer that can act on tool outputs, while Chatwoot produces customer-support content and reports. If Chatwoot text is fed into CrewAI as authoritative input, CrewAI may execute downstream actions or generate responses without verification. That creates a strong cascade from support content into operational actions, and no built-in verification is shown.
conditions: IF Chatwoot transcripts or reports are used as CrewAI task inputs, CrewAI may treat them as authoritative.
IF CrewAI agents are allowed to act on those inputs without review, downstream errors can propagate.
mitigations: Require human approval before CrewAI acts on Chatwoot-derived content.
Add a verification step that checks Chatwoot facts against source records.
Limit CrewAI to drafting, not executing, customer-facing actions.
Log every Chatwoot-to-CrewAI handoff.
requires-engineering: implement source-citation validation in the orchestrator.

E_compliance.rationale: Chatwoot clearly handles customer data and messages, while CrewAI handles developer-passed crew data and can send it to model providers and tools. The profiles do not specify residency or retention controls, so a compliance mismatch is plausible if regulated customer data is routed into CrewAI. Because the exact jurisdictional mismatch is undocumented, medium is the safer choice.
conditions: IF regulated customer data from Chatwoot is passed into CrewAI, compliance obligations apply.
IF CrewAI model providers or tools retain prompts, retention mismatch may occur.
mitigations: Do not pass regulated data into CrewAI unless approved.
Redact customer identifiers before handoff.
Review provider retention settings before enabling runs.
Keep audit logs of all data transfers.
requires-engineering: map residency and retention controls end to end.
